entries.title: Cell Membrane with Moving Ion Channels
entries.description: A large transparent sphere acts as a cell membrane with colored “ion channel” cylinders that open and close, letting small charged spheres drift through, bounce, and leave trails while a simple meter shows inside vs. outside ion counts.

entries.title: 3D Cell with Organelles and Cytoplasmic Flow
entries.description: A semi-transparent cell sphere contains a nucleus, mitochondria, vesicles, and ribosomes, where vesicles float along curved paths, gently collide and bounce off organelles, and leave faint trails while labels hover over each structure.

entries.title: Cell Division (Mitosis) Animation
entries.description: A single cell sphere with a central duplicated chromosome cluster stretches, forms spindle fibers (thin rods) that pull chromosome spheres apart, and the whole cell pinches into two daughter cells that detach and drift slightly apart.

entries.title: Vesicle Trafficking Along Microtubules
entries.description: Long microtubule “tracks” radiate from a central centrosome, with small vesicle spheres “walking” along them via stepwise motion, sometimes detaching, switching tracks, and fusing with a target membrane sphere that changes color where fusion occurs.

entries.title: Endocytosis and Exocytosis at the Membrane
entries.description: A cell sphere with many small external particles shows membrane regions curving in to wrap and pinch off endocytic vesicles, while internal vesicles move outward and merge with the membrane to release particles that scatter and slowly diffuse away.

entries.title: Mitochondria as Dynamic Power Stations
entries.description: Multiple elongated mitochondria shapes inside a cell gently move, split, and merge, with glowing particles streaming into them and dimmer particles emitted, while their brightness fluctuates to show changing activity and a label shows “ATP level.”

entries.title: Immune Cell Chasing a Bacterium

entries.title: Calcium Wave Signaling in a Cell
entries.description: A network of thin internal compartments (ER-like tubes) inside a cell lights up with a traveling calcium wave: small bright particles rapidly spread, bounce at boundaries, then are reabsorbed into pumps, as a color bar tracks local calcium concentration over time.

Here are strong **biological cell simulation inputs** you can plug into your prompt:

1. **Cell Membrane with Moving Ion Channels**
   A large transparent sphere acts as a cell membrane with colored “ion channel” cylinders that open and close, letting small charged spheres drift through, bounce, and leave trails while a simple meter shows inside vs. outside ion counts.

2. **3D Cell with Organelles and Cytoplasmic Flow**
   A semi-transparent cell sphere contains a nucleus, mitochondria, vesicles, and ribosomes, where vesicles float along curved paths, gently collide and bounce off organelles, and leave faint trails while labels hover over each structure.

3. **Cell Division (Mitosis) Animation**
   A single cell sphere with a central duplicated chromosome cluster stretches, forms spindle fibers (thin rods) that pull chromosome spheres apart, and the whole cell pinches into two daughter cells that detach and drift slightly apart.

4. **Vesicle Trafficking Along Microtubules**
   Long microtubule “tracks” radiate from a central centrosome, with small vesicle spheres “walking” along them via stepwise motion, sometimes detaching, switching tracks, and fusing with a target membrane sphere that changes color where fusion occurs.

5. **Endocytosis and Exocytosis at the Membrane**
   A cell sphere with many small external particles shows membrane regions curving in to wrap and pinch off endocytic vesicles, while internal vesicles move outward and merge with the membrane to release particles that scatter and slowly diffuse away.

6. **Mitochondria as Dynamic Power Stations**
   Multiple elongated mitochondria shapes inside a cell gently move, split, and merge, with glowing particles streaming into them and dimmer particles emitted, while their brightness fluctuates to show changing activity and a label shows “ATP level.”

7. **Immune Cell Chasing a Bacterium**
   A deformable immune cell blob slowly moves toward a smaller bacterium capsule, extending and retracting pseudopod-like protrusions; upon collision it wraps around and engulfs the bacterium, which fades as digestion particles swirl inside.

8. **Calcium Wave Signaling in a Cell**
   A network of thin internal compartments (ER-like tubes) inside a cell lights up with a traveling calcium wave: small bright particles rapidly spread, bounce at boundaries, then are reabsorbed into pumps, as a color bar tracks local calcium concentration over time.

9. **3D Cell Cycle Clock with Growing Cell**
   A single cell sphere gradually grows in size and changes color as it progresses through labeled phases (G1, S, G2, M) on a circular “clock” ring beside it; during S phase tiny DNA dots duplicate, and during M phase the cell splits into two smaller spheres.

10. **Cell Swarm Communication in Tissue**
    Dozens of small cells float and gently jostle in a transparent box, emitting and absorbing colored signal particles; when one cell receives above-threshold signals, it glows brighter and triggers neighboring cells to light up in a spreading wave.
